2 Oct — Villa El Salvador, Lima: A driver for the Lipetsa ('Los Triangulos') bus company was shot dead on his route in what police believe was an extortion ('cobro de cupos') attack; a four-year-old child was also wounded by gunfire in Lima/Callao the same weekend.
5 Oct — Independencia, Lima: A colectivo driver was shot dead by two gunmen on a motorcycle in front of his home as his wife and young son looked on.

7 Oct — Lima: Transport unions representing about 90% of Lima-Callao operators said they would decide on 9 Oct whether to call a national strike, citing 85 sector deaths in 2026; Congress has granted the government 20 of the 66 delegated legislative powers it requested.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Recurring deadly violence by extortion networks against the transport sector, together with the September killing of a gubernatorial candidate, meets the HIGH definition, while there is no territorial loss of state control that would justify CRITICAL. The 60-day state of emergency in Lima and Callao declared on 28 August expires in late October and is likely to be renewed, possibly with a wider military role as President Fujimori pushes to treat criminal networks as terrorists. Over 90 days, expect continued weekly killings of drivers, a probable transport strike that would paralyse Lima, and election-related threats ahead of the regional vote. Upgrade triggers: further attacks on candidates or officials, a mass-casualty extortion bombing, or clashes during a strike.

countries.name: Bolivia
incidents: 28 Sep — Nationwide: The Confederation of Drivers' 24-hour withdrawal against Supreme Decree 5716 (diesel at Bs 17.95/litre) was only partially observed: transport stopped in Santa Cruz, Chuquisaca, Potosi and Oruro but ran normally in La Paz and El Alto; no clashes were reported.

29–30 Sep — La Paz: Government-driver talks ended without agreement but drivers ruled out further protests pending cost studies, while urban teachers marched in La Paz and other cities against the decree and the government's economic measures.
1 Oct — Nationwide: Bolivian gas distributors announced a strike over the diesel price rise.

5 Oct — La Paz: The government agreed with the heavy-transport federation FENCOOTRANS to facilitate direct diesel imports for the sector's own use, after earlier transitional freight-rate deals with tanker operators to keep fuel distribution at 100%.
countries.coa: Downgraded to MODERATE. The removal of the diesel subsidy has produced strikes and marches, but so far without road blockades, clashes or casualties, and the government is defusing sector by sector through targeted deals while the state of exception (to 17 December) deters blockades. Over the next 90 days, expect further staggered sectoral strikes (gas distributors, teachers, farmers) and fare disputes as transport costs are passed on, with the risk of escalation concentrated around any attempt by Santa Cruz agricultural producers or Morales-aligned groups to cut roads. Return to HIGH if multi-day blockades resume, security forces clear roads with force causing casualties, or protests turn into calls for President Paz's resignation as in May–June, when 14 people died.

countries.name: Dominican Republic
incidents: 3–4 Oct — Nationwide/Dajabon: The General Directorate of Migration reported 1,171 foreigners detained in nationwide operations as of 3 October and deported 302 Haitians through the Dajabon crossing on 4 October, continuing a pace of more than 250,000 deportations in the first seven months of 2026.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. No organised armed violence or significant security incidents were reported in the window; activity is limited to routine migration enforcement and crime. Over the next 90 days, expect mass deportations and border-wall construction to continue at record pace, with a risk of new displacement toward the border if GSF operations and gang reprisals intensify in Artibonite and the Centre department. The Dominican Republic will remain a cocaine transit point with continued joint US maritime interdictions. The main risks are diplomatic and humanitarian friction with Haiti rather than internal instability.

countries.name: Jamaica
incidents: 5 Oct — Christiana, Manchester: Police shot dead 26-year-old Raheem 'Richie' Nelson in an alleged confrontation at a bar while searching for a murder suspect; police said he was armed, was on bail for a 2024 murder and was wanted for a July killing in Clarendon.
6 Oct — Harbour View, Kingston: A dispute between two businessmen over a shared boatyard ended with 63-year-old Paul Thompson allegedly shooting the other man twice before being shot dead by police.

7 Oct — Nationwide: Figures cited by the Jamaica Observer show 407 murders so far in 2026 (down 24% year on year) against 231 deaths at the hands of security forces, as a rights advocate warned that Jamaicans are increasingly afraid of the police.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. Violence remains criminal rather than organised political or armed-group violence, and murders are on course for a historic low. The main source of tension is the very high rate of security-force killings, now more than half the number of criminal murders, and disputed accounts from communities, which INDECOM continues to investigate. Over 90 days, expect further contested police shootings, localized roadblock protests and rights criticism, with the government firmly backing the security forces. Watch for any escalation of protests into sustained unrest in Kingston/St Andrew or western parishes, and for late-season hurricane impacts as a parallel hazard.
